attempted_claim: Let d ≥ 6, 0 < b < 2, α = (4−2b)/(d−2), and consider i∂_t u + Δu + |x|^{−b}|u|^{α}u = 0, u|_{t=0} = u_0 ∈ Ḣ¹(R^d). Let W be the positive radial ground state solving ΔW + |x|^{−b}W^{α+1} = 0. Do there exist radial solutions W^± with E(W^±) = E(W), defined at least on [0,∞), with ‖W^±(t)−W‖_{Ḣ¹} ≤ Ce^{−ct} for t > 0, ‖∇W^−(t)‖_2 < ‖∇W‖_2 with W^− scattering backward in time, and ‖∇W^+(t)‖_2 > ‖∇W‖_2? And does every maximal Ḣ¹ threshold solution with E(u_0) = E(W) satisfy: (a) if ‖∇u_0‖_2 < ‖∇W‖_2 then either u scatters in both time directions or u = W^− up to symmetries; (b) if ‖∇u_0‖_2 = ‖∇W‖_2 then u = W up to symmetries; (c) if ‖∇u_0‖_2 > ‖∇W‖_2 and u_0 is radial in L², then either the lifespan is finite or u = W^+ up to symmetries?
decisive_failure: No complete-target route remains: the Holder-only nonlinearity defeats the standard W+- contraction, and the spectral/nondegeneracy plus d>=6 singular-weight profile/stability inputs are missing. Session diagnostics (ground-state verification, remainder scaling) are recorded but claim no original result.
